blocks.content: The simplest of these sequential adjustments is Holm's method (Holm 1979). The first step is to order the $p$ values for the $n$ hypotheses being tested from smallest to largest, $p(1) p(2) p(n)$, and let $H(i)$ be the hypothesis associated with $p(i)$. One proceeds with Holm's method as follows: (i) If $ p(1) > /n $, accept all $ n $ null hypotheses (i.e., none are declared significant).
(ii) If $ p(1) /n $, reject $ H(1) $ [i.e., $ H(1) $ is declared significant], and consider $ H(2) $.
(iv) If $ p(2) /(n-1) $, reject $ H(2) $ and move onto $ H(3) $.
(v) Proceed with rejecting hypotheses until reaching the first i such that $ p(i) > /(n - i + 1) $.
We can also apply Holm’s method using Equation A4.3a—namely, $ = 1 - (1 -)^ 1/n $, the Dunn-Šidák correction—in place of $ = /n $.
